- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 2–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often lags — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in next 2–3 periods.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if 30d forecast is below 65.0, add 0.5–1.5% to correct for bias toward lower prices.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.4+), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before final output.
